title: Brandenburg-Prussia
capsule: Brandenburg-Prussia denotes the composite Hohenzollern state formed when Elector John Sigismund inherited the Duchy of Prussia in 1618, linking the Mark of Brandenburg on the middle Elbe-Oder with the fief in East Prussia that lay outside the Holy Roman Empire. The Great Elector Frederick William (1640–1688) transformed the scattered territories into a cohesive militarized state, defeating Sweden at Fehrbellin in 1675 and establishing a standing army that would define Prussian statecraft. His son Frederick III obtained the title 'King in Prussia' from Emperor Leopold I in 1701, crowning himself Frederick I at Königsberg; from that moment the state was conventionally called the Kingdom of Prussia, ending the Brandenburg-Prussia period.
